prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production sprite art for an existing 2D water nest growth animation. Both input images are strict STYLE, PALETTE, MATERIAL and CAMERA references only: glossy cyan/turquoise magical water, creamy aqua highlights, dark teal contour, painterly clean mobile-game shading, slightly top-down isometric view. Generate a transparent-background square atlas containing EIGHT isolated WATER ACTION key drawings arranged in an exact 4 columns by 2 rows grid, read left to right then top to bottom. Each drawing stays entirely inside its cell with generous clear margins. All drawings belong to ONE fluid eruption from a pool; do NOT draw the nest rim or the base pool, only the moving water above it, with a small flattened attachment foot where connected. Each connected drawing has the same centered base and bottom baseline. Row1 cell1: very low rounded pressure mound, flattened wide dome. Cell2: gathered taller bulbous water mound, smooth single fluid surface. Cell3: vertical takeoff water column with round drop head and narrowing attached base, NOT an animal or snake, no sideways curve. Cell4: small compact detached round globule flying upward, with one short tapered lower tail; roughly half the width of the mound. Row2 cell1: same globule descending, moderately vertically stretched and smaller than the mound, no detached particles. Cell2: impact splash crown, low broad symmetrical fluid cup with two short rounded crests curling outward, center open, low flat attachment base. Cell3: flattened spreading impact crown, crests half as tall, oval center open. Cell4: very low circular ripple mound, almost settled, flattened ellipse. Keep a coherent silhouette progression and identical lighting. Shapes should feel liquid, energetic and clean, suitable for an anticipation -> quick jump -> sudden larger settled pool transition. No random floating droplets, no bubbles inside, no sparkles, no magic rings, no faces, no text, no labels, no borders, no background, no shadows cast outside the water. Actual transparent alpha. These are final source drawings to be cropped, registered and animated in the game, not a presentation sheet.
